Every day, Nigerian businesses sell, restock and pay their staff. And most of it lives in a notebook, a bank alert, and a WhatsApp chat.
Meet CACU. One place to sell, track your stock, run your team, and keep real books, without needing to know accounting.
Setting up takes minutes. Name your business, tell CACU whether you sell products, services, or both, and it shapes itself around how you work.
Add your products and services. Stock only changes through recorded movements, and big adjustments wait for an owner's approval. So nothing quietly disappears.
At the till, prices come from your catalogue, not from whoever is holding the phone. Ring up a cash or transfer sale, and it's recorded the moment you confirm.
Selling on credit? Issue an invoice, record part payments as they come in, and always know exactly who still owes you.
Supplier bills, payments and everyday expenses work the same way. Made a mistake? An owner or admin reverses it, with a reason. Nothing is ever deleted.
When you're ready, Start your books asks plain questions. How much cash is in the till? Who owes you? Who do you owe? You approve the answers, and your books begin.
From then on, every sale, receipt and bill posts balanced double-entry, automatically, on a standard Nigerian chart of accounts reviewed by a chartered accountant.
Trial balance. General ledger. Profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow, with comparatives, ready as PDF or Excel. And your stock is valued at weighted-average cost.
Invite your team as admins, editors or viewers. Keep staff records, track attendance, and prepare payroll on the 2026 Nigeria Tax Act bands, with every run approved by an owner or admin.
Behind it all, every business's data stays separate, posted records can't be quietly changed, and uploads are checked before anyone sees them.
And this is just the beginning. Here's what's coming next.
Transfers that wait until you confirm the money really arrived. An installable app that keeps selling when the network drops. And three plans, Founder, Innovator and Empire, paid through Paystack.
Purchase orders and stock transfers. Bookings with deposits and WhatsApp reminders. Cashier shifts, roles for cashiers and accountants, bank reconciliation, budgets, and VAT.

Ask CACU how much profit you made this month, and get the answer from your real books. See how ready your business is for funding, and share it with a lender only when you choose. Then payroll posting, e-invoicing, and new countries.
CACU. Sell. CACU keeps the books.
